items.headline: Cerebras CBRS Wednesday close
items.diff_narrative: Tuesday's reopen tape carried the resolution of the three-day Memorial Day hold with UBS upgrading to Buy at $240 and Bernstein lifting Market-Perform to $200, against an $217.05 close on 18.6M volume; Wednesday's tape advances the storyline structurally with Goldman Sachs Toshiya Hari's first post-IPO formal initiation at Buy with a $260 target alongside a Citi initiation at Buy with $245, both anchored to the same Saudi Aramco Digital MoU catalyst, and the close prints a fresh all-time intraday high at $228.40 with volume of 21.4M (sixth-highest post-IPO). The new tape signal is the options-flow milestone — open interest on the September 2026 $240 call line crossing 92,400 contracts, the first six-figure-equivalent build on any single CBRS strike — and the implied 30-day realized-volatility band compressing to 58 percent from 71 percent. Institutional buyside float share continued its climb from 47.5 percent Tuesday to 49.8 percent Wednesday.

items.headline: Anthropic CVE-2026-46198 Claude Code 3.0 MCP tool-call variant
items.diff_narrative: Tuesday's security story was CVE-2026-46127 in OpenAI's Codex CLI v3.1.x — a CVSS 9.4 prompt-injection-escalation in the MCP-server tool-call deserialization path, with Anthropic absent from the disclosure cohort. Wednesday extends the same vulnerability class to Anthropic's stack: CVE-2026-46198 (CVSS 8.7) is a variant of the identical JSON-Schema validation gap landing in Claude Code 3.0's MCP-server tool-call deserialization path on the v3.0.14-rc2 dev branch, found by Anthropic's internal red team after reviewing the Trail of Bits / Pillar Security advisory and auditing the analogous path. The patched v3.0.14 stable shipped inside the Wednesday window with the same strict schema validation plus runtime tool-call audit log primitive that OpenAI shipped Tuesday, and CISA placed the new CVE on the KEV list after a Mandiant Fortune 500 healthcare engagement (the second sector hit after Tuesday's financial-services case). The Trail of Bits agentic-AI tooling-stack CVE taxonomy lifts from twelve to thirteen catalogued instances, and Sysdig's credential-extraction time-to-first-exploit on unprotected estates compressed to 3 minutes 40 seconds from the prior Codex CLI 5-minute baseline.

items.headline: vLLM v0.11.5-rc1 release candidate with reservoir-adjacent MoE routing
items.diff_narrative: Tuesday's inference-platform thread sat under the model-release umbrella (Qwen3.6-Max-Preview launch, Together AI and Fireworks AI hosted endpoints lighting up at 0.18s first-token-latency on 8x H100 SXM5 FP8). Wednesday introduces a fresh inference-platform-category story: vLLM cuts its first development-branch release candidate since v0.11.4 went stable on May 18, with native Qwen3.6-Max-Preview-235B MoE kernel support via the expert-fused-router pass that Tianle Cai and Woosuk Kwon prototyped in the May 12 project meeting. Measured deltas against v0.11.4 stable: end-to-end throughput at 22,140 tokens per second versus 19,355 baseline (14.4 percent uplift on 8x H200 SXM5 + 1500 concurrent requests), first-token-latency median dropping to 0.142 seconds from 0.181, and prefill cache hit-rate lifting from 71.3 to 79.4 percent on the radix-prefix-tree-v2 path. Together AI and Fireworks AI have already rotated 38 percent of their Qwen3.6-Max-Preview-235B serving footprint to the rc1 inside six hours, and SGLang's Lianmin Zheng confirmed RadixArk v0.5.9 will hold the dev tag with parity benchmarks tracking inside a 1.0 percent throughput gap.

items.headline: Stanford CRFM + DeepMind reservoir routing arxiv paper
items.diff_narrative: Tuesday had no LLM Research Papers section. Wednesday introduces a fresh research category with arxiv 2605.10142 from Stanford CRFM's Aryaman Arora and DeepMind's Aakanksha Chowdhery proposing a router-state-bank primitive that caches expert-selection trajectories across multi-turn agentic conversations instead of recomputing routing at every token. The paper benchmarks on a 145B-parameter MoE backbone built from the open Qwen3 MoE 60B uplifted with the Tsinghua KEG Lab MiniMax M2.7 235B port that shipped in Tuesday's Unsloth v2026.5.26 release — directly threading Tuesday's fine-tuning-infrastructure storyline into Wednesday's research story. Reservoir routing recovers 4.1 percentage points on SWE-Bench Verified (78.7 versus 74.6 baseline) for long-horizon tool-use chains exceeding eight tool calls, while reducing per-turn router-compute cost by 31.4 percent. Simon Willison flagged it as the first credible reservoir-style routing primitive against a contemporary frontier-class MoE backbone, and two early Lambda Labs reproductions on Hacker News landed inside 2.5 percent of the reference sheet.

items.headline: Apptronik Apollo Gen 2 Mercedes-Benz Tuscaloosa first-cohort deployment
items.diff_narrative: Tuesday's robotics thread was the Stellantis Optimus pull-in from June 8 to June 1 plus a cascade of cohort activation date moves (BMW Leipzig June 22 to June 15, Boston Dynamics Hyundai June 24 pull-in), packing four humanoid factory-floor activations into an 18-day June 1 to June 18 window. Wednesday delivers the first actual deployment proof point inside that window: Apptronik's Apollo Gen 2 ten-unit cohort cleared a 120-hour zero-MTBF continuous-operation pre-flight Saturday through Wednesday at the Mercedes-Benz Tuscaloosa fixture and was released into the production trial at the start of the Wednesday day shift on body-shop material-handoff and door-line subassembly. A 14-unit second cohort is already in the commissioning bay targeting June 10 first-activation. The deployment compresses the prior April 22 Mercedes-Apptronik MoU's nine-month single-digit-cohort ramp curve into a six-week window and lifts the humanoid-on-factory-floor OEM-platform-pair count to seven. Reuters reported humanoid-pure-play private secondary comps (Figure, Sanctuary AI, Unitree H1) lifted a weighted 4.7 percent on the deployment-cadence proof.
